statements.text: a driver SHOULD use low beams WHEN the driver is less than 60 m behind another vehicle UNLESS the driver is passing the vehicle

sources.quote: Use your low beams when you are less than 60 metres behind another vehicle unless you are passing it.

statements.note: The sentence's main content is a headlight rule; the passing-relevant part is the UNLESS clause, which lifts the low-beam requirement while passing. The statement keeps the full rule with its same-passage exception as an UNLESS clause.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD keep to the right of the road OR in the right-hand lane on a multi-lane road UNLESS the driver wants to turn left OR the driver wants to pass another vehicle

sources.quote: Keep to the right of the road or in the right-hand lane on multi-lane roads unless you want to turn left or pass another vehicle.

flags.span: Keep to the right of the road
flags.note: A flat command stating the basic rule of the road could be a legal duty, but the passage has no legal wording, so it stays SHOULD.

statements.note: The keep-right duty is not itself passing, but its UNLESS clause is the only passing content in the batch: passing another vehicle is a permitted reason to leave the right lane, so the whole rule is kept as one statement rather than split.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk BECAUSE a stopped vehicle may be a clue that a pedestrian is crossing

sources.quote: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. A stopped vehicle may be a clue that a pedestrian is crossing.

statements.text: FACT a cyclist can use any part of the lane if [?necessary] for safety, such as to discourage passing where the lane is too narrow to be shared [?safely]

sources.quote: However, they can use any part of the lane if necessary for safety, such as to:
Discourage passing where the lane is too narrow to be shared safely

flags.note: No measure of when using any part of the lane is necessary.
No measure of how wide a lane must be to be shared.

statements.note: "They" refers to cyclists per the heading. Only item 3 of the lead's list is in this batch, so only that example is extracted.

statements.text: a driver MUST maintain a minimum distance of 1 m between the driver's vehicle and a cyclist where [?practical] WHEN passing a cyclist IF VIOLATED a fine AND 2 demerit points

sources.quote: When passing a cyclist, drivers of motor vehicles must maintain a minimum distance of one metre, where practical between their vehicle and the cyclist.
(See Diagram 2-11.) Failure to do so may result in a fine and an additional two demerit points on the driver’s record.
bike lane adjacent to parking bays

flags.note: No test for when the 1 m distance is practical; the duty is conditional on practicality.

statements.note: The handbook addresses "drivers of motor vehicles"; the role is written as a driver. "Failure to do so" in m57 refers to the duty in m56, so the penalty joins that rule. Diagram 2-11 is cited because m57 points to it.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD change lanes to pass a cyclist WHEN passing a cyclist AND it is [?possible] to change lanes

sources.quote: Whenever possible, you should change lanes to pass.

flags.note: No measure of when changing lanes is possible.

statements.note: The condition "passing a cyclist" comes from the heading Cyclists, which this item sits under.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT sound the horn [?unnecessarily] WHEN passing a cyclist BECAUSE it may frighten the cyclist and cause them to lose control

sources.quote: Do not sound your horn unnecessarily when you are overtaking a cyclist. It may frighten them and cause them to lose control.

flags.note: No measure of when sounding the horn is necessary.
The handbook says "overtaking" here and "passing" elsewhere for the same act; the statement uses "passing".

statements.text: a driver SHOULD tap the horn quickly and lightly WHEN the driver feels the driver must use the horn AND passing a cyclist WHILE the driver is still [?some distance] away from the cyclist

sources.quote: Do not sound your horn unnecessarily when you are overtaking a cyclist. It may frighten them and cause them to lose control. If you feel that you must use your horn, tap it quickly and lightly while you are still some distance away from the cyclist.

flags.note: No distance given for still being some distance away.
The handbook says "overtaking" here and "passing" elsewhere for the same act; the statement uses "passing".

statements.note: "Must" in "feels that you must use your horn" describes a felt necessity, not a legal duty; the force is the imperative "tap". The "passing a cyclist" condition comes from the first sentence of the passage.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT cut in front of a large vehicle [?closely] WHEN passing a large vehicle BECAUSE it is discourteous and dangerous, and it reduces the space cushion a large vehicle requires in order to stop [?safely]

sources.quote: When passing a large vehicle, do not cut in front closely. Not only is this discourteous, it is dangerous; it reduces the space cushion large vehicles require in order to stop safely.

flags.note: No measure of how close to the front of a large vehicle is too close.
No measure of the space cushion a large vehicle needs to stop safely.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD allow [?more room] WHEN passing a large vehicle

sources.quote: Allow more room when passing a large vehicle.

flags.note: No measure of how much extra room to allow.

statements.text: FACT a large vehicle can create heavy air turbulence that may affect the driver's ability to control the driver's vehicle WHEN the driver is passing a large vehicle

sources.quote: 6. Turbulence - Due to various factors such as air pressure and airflow, a large vehicle can create heavy air turbulence. This may affect your ability to control your vehicle when passing a large one.

statements.note: "This" in the passage refers to the air turbulence; it is resolved in the statement.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD stay [?well back] WHEN following farm machinery

sources.quote: Stay well back and do not pass until it is safe to do so.

flags.note: No distance given for how far back to stay.

statements.note: The road user (farm machinery) comes from the heading.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass farm machinery UNTIL it is [?safe] to do so

statements.note: The road user (farm machinery) comes from the heading.

sources.quote: You may not pass on the left shoulder, paved or not.

statements.text: FACT [?Most] passing is done on the left

sources.quote: Most passing is done on the left.

flags.note: Generalization with no proportion given.

statements.text: a driver MAY pass on the right WHEN the road is a multi-lane road OR the road is a one-way road OR the driver is overtaking a streetcar OR the driver is overtaking a vehicle turning left

sources.quote: You may pass on the right on multi-lane or one-way roads and when overtaking a streetcar or a left-turning vehicle.

statements.text: FACT passing on the right can be more dangerous than passing on the left

sources.quote: Passing on the right can be more dangerous than passing on the left.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD wait for the vehicle in front to move to the right WHEN the driver is in the left most lane AND a slower vehicle is in front of the driver

sources.quote: If you are driving in the left most lane with a slower vehicle in front of you, wait for the vehicle to move to the right.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT suddenly change lanes and pass on the right WHEN the driver is in the left most lane AND a slower vehicle is in front of the driver BECAUSE the driver in front may realize the driver wants to pass and move to the right at the same time the driver does

sources.quote: Do not suddenly change lanes and pass on the right; the driver in front may realize you want to pass and move to the right at the same time you do.

statements.text: a driver MUST pass a streetcar on the right UNLESS the driver is driving on a one-way road

sources.quote: You must pass streetcars on the right unless you are driving on a one-way road.

statements.text: a driver MUST stay at least 2 m behind the rear doors where passengers are getting off or on WHEN the driver is at a streetcar stop UNLESS the stop has an area set aside for streetcar passengers

sources.quote: At streetcar stops, stay at least two metres behind the rear doors where passengers are getting off or on. This rule does not apply at stops where an area has been set aside for streetcar passengers.
a vehicle stopped the required two metres behind the rear doors of a stopped streetcar

statements.note: The passage calls the instruction a rule, giving it legal force.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD pass an area set aside for streetcar passengers at a [?reasonable] speed AND be prepared for pedestrians to make [?sudden or unexpected] moves WHEN the driver is passing the area

sources.quote: Always pass these areas at a reasonable speed and be prepared for pedestrians to make sudden or unexpected moves.
This rule does not apply at stops where an area has been set aside for streetcar passengers.

flags.note: No speed measure is given.
No measure of suddenness or unexpectedness is given.

statements.note: "These areas" are resolved as the set-aside streetcar passenger areas from m63.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass [?the smaller vehicle] WHEN the driver is making a left turn UNTIL the smaller vehicle moves right

sources.quote: Wait for the smaller vehicle to move right before you pass.

flags.note: The batch does not identify the smaller vehicle or its relationship to the driver.

statements.note: The condition making a left turn comes from the heading; before you pass is written as a prohibition with UNTIL.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pull up beside [?one of these vehicles] to make the left turn at the same time as the vehicle makes the turn WHEN the driver is making a left turn behind the vehicle

sources.quote: If you are making a left turn behind one of these vehicles, do not pull up beside it to make your turn at the same time.

flags.note: The batch does not include the list or description that these vehicles refers to.

statements.note: The pronoun it is resolved as the vehicle; the same time is understood as the vehicle making the turn.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD stay behind [?one of these vehicles] WHEN the driver is making a left turn behind the vehicle UNTIL the way is clear

sources.quote: Stay behind and turn when the way is clear.
If you are making a left turn behind one of these vehicles, do not pull up beside it to make your turn at the same time.

flags.note: The batch does not include the list or description that these vehicles refers to.

statements.note: The object of stay behind and the condition behind one of these vehicles are taken from the neighbouring sentence c6.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD make the left turn WHEN the driver is making a left turn behind [?one of these vehicles] AND the way is clear

sources.quote: Stay behind and turn when the way is clear.
If you are making a left turn behind one of these vehicles, do not pull up beside it to make your turn at the same time.

flags.note: The batch does not include the list or description that these vehicles refers to.

statements.note: The condition making a left turn behind one of these vehicles is taken from c6; turn is expanded to make the left turn from the heading.

statements.text: a driver MUST NOT use [?these left-turn lanes] for passing

sources.quote: These left-turn lanes are not to be used for passing.

flags.note: The batch does not identify which left-turn lanes are meant.

statements.note: The passive prohibition is written as a rule for the driver using the lanes.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD keep to the right lane WHEN driving on a freeway

sources.quote: Traffic should keep to the right, using the left lanes for passing.
Drive in the right-hand lane when possible.
Get into the habit of driving in the right lane, leaving the other lanes clear for passing.

flags.note: m33 adds the qualifier 'when possible'; m32 and m34 state the rule without it.

statements.note: Three passages state the same right-lane rule; m33 softens it with 'when possible'.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD use the left lanes for passing WHEN driving on a freeway

sources.quote: Traffic should keep to the right, using the left lanes for passing.
Get into the habit of driving in the right lane, leaving the other lanes clear for passing.

statements.note: m33 gives a more specific version for multi-lane freeways (s3).

statements.text: a driver SHOULD use the far left lane of a multi-lane freeway to pass traffic moving slower than the speed limit

sources.quote: Use the far left lane of a multi-lane freeway to pass traffic moving slower than the speed limit, but don't stay there.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT stay in the far left lane of a multi-lane freeway

sources.quote: Use the far left lane of a multi-lane freeway to pass traffic moving slower than the speed limit, but don't stay there.

statements.text: a driver of a large truck MUST NOT travel in the far left lane WHEN on a freeway with 3 or more lanes in each direction

sources.quote: On many freeways with three or more lanes in each direction, large trucks cannot travel in the far left lane and must use the lane to the right for passing.

flags.note: The handbook says 'many freeways' with 3 or more lanes in each direction, not all such freeways; it is unclear which freeways are covered.

statements.note: "Cannot travel" is a legal prohibition in the traffic-law context, so the force is MUST NOT.

statements.text: a driver of a large truck MUST use the lane to the right for passing WHEN on a freeway with 3 or more lanes in each direction

sources.quote: On many freeways with three or more lanes in each direction, large trucks cannot travel in the far left lane and must use the lane to the right for passing.

flags.note: The handbook says 'many freeways' with 3 or more lanes in each direction, not all such freeways; it is unclear which freeways are covered.

statements.text: a driver MUST reduce the speed of the vehicle AND proceed with [?caution] WHEN (the driver approaches an emergency vehicle that is stopped with its red lights flashing OR the driver approaches an emergency vehicle that is stopped with its red and blue lights flashing OR the driver approaches a tow truck that is stopped with its amber lights flashing) AND the emergency vehicle or tow truck is in the same direction of the driver's travel

sources.quote: Reacting to a stopped emergency vehicle or tow truck

When approaching any emergency vehicle that is stopped with its red, or red and blue, lights flashing or a tow truck with its amber lights flashing in the same direction of your travel, you are required to reduce the speed of your vehicle and proceed with caution.

flags.note: No level of caution is given.

statements.text: a driver MUST move into a lane away from the emergency vehicle or tow truck WHEN (the driver approaches an emergency vehicle that is stopped with its red lights flashing OR the driver approaches an emergency vehicle that is stopped with its red and blue lights flashing OR the driver approaches a tow truck that is stopped with its amber lights flashing) AND the emergency vehicle or tow truck is in the same direction of the driver's travel AND the roadway has two or more lanes of traffic in the same direction of the driver's travel AND it is [?safe] to do so

sources.quote: Reacting to a stopped emergency vehicle or tow truck

When the roadway has two or more lanes of traffic in the same direction of your travel, you are required to move into a lane away from the emergency vehicle or tow truck, if safe to do so, in addition to reducing the speed of your vehicle and proceeding with caution.
Reacting to a stopped emergency vehicle or tow truck

When approaching any emergency vehicle that is stopped with its red, or red and blue, lights flashing or a tow truck with its amber lights flashing in the same direction of your travel, you are required to reduce the speed of your vehicle and proceed with caution.

flags.note: No test is given for when moving into another lane is safe.

statements.note: The m79 duty is stated as in addition to the reduce-speed and proceed-with-caution duty in s1; the stopped-vehicle condition is taken from m78.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass another vehicle WHEN driving in fog

sources.quote: Avoid passing, changing lanes and crossing traffic.
Don't pass other vehicles or speed up suddenly.

statements.note: m45 and m47 state the same advice for fog, so they make one statement. 'Changing lanes', 'crossing traffic', 'speed up suddenly' and the patience reminders are not about passing.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass another vehicle WHEN driving in a whiteout

sources.quote: Avoid passing, changing lanes and crossing traffic.

statements.note: The condition 'in a whiteout' comes from the heading 'Whiteouts › DO'.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT speed up to pass a vehicle moving slowly WHEN driving in fog

sources.quote: Don't speed up to pass a vehicle moving slowly or to get away from a vehicle that is following too closely.

statements.note: The alternative purpose 'to get away from a vehicle that is following too closely' is about a close follower, not overtaking, so it is not extracted.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT attempt to pass a vehicle moving slowly WHEN driving in a whiteout

sources.quote: Don't attempt to pass a vehicle moving slowly or to get away from a vehicle that is following too closely.

statements.note: The alternative purpose 'to get away from a vehicle that is following too closely' is about a close follower, not overtaking, so it is not extracted.

statements.text: FACT on freeways, several snow plows may be staggered across the road, clearing all lanes at the same time by passing a ridge of snow from plow to plow

sources.quote: On freeways, several snow plows may be staggered across the road, clearing all lanes at the same time by passing a ridge of snow from plow to plow.

statements.note: 'Passing' here means the plows transfer the ridge of snow to each other, not overtaking; the fact describes the situation the plow rule applies in.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT try to pass between the snow plows WHEN the road is a freeway AND several snow plows are staggered across the road BECAUSE it is extremely dangerous: there is not [?enough] room to pass [?safely] AND the ridge of wet snow can throw the vehicle out of control

sources.quote: Do not try to pass between them. This is extremely dangerous because there is not enough room to pass safely, and the ridge of wet snow can throw your vehicle out of control.

flags.note: No measure of how much room is enough.
No objective standard for passing safely.

statements.note: 'Them' refers to the snow plows. 'Do not try' is a plain command with a danger warning but no legal wording, so it stays advice.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass on the road WHEN a "do not pass on this road" sign is posted on the road

sources.quote: a regulatory sign
Do not pass on this road.

flags.note: A regulatory sign likely has legal force, but the batch does not state that regulatory signs must be obeyed.

statements.note: The sign caption is a plain imperative in the provided batch, so it is kept as advice with an M flag.

statements.text: a driver MUST keep right WHEN the driver is in [?slow] traffic AND the road is a multi-lane road AND a "slow traffic on multi-lane roads must keep right" sign is posted

sources.quote: Slow traffic on multi-lane roads must keep right.
a regulatory sign

flags.note: No speed or rate defining slow traffic is given.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD keep to the right lane WHEN a "keep to the right lane except when passing on two-lane sections where climbing or passing lanes are provided" sign is posted UNLESS the driver is passing on a two-lane section where a climbing lane or a passing lane is provided

sources.quote: a regulatory sign
Keep to the right lane except when passing on two-lane sections where climbing or passing lanes are provided.

flags.note: A regulatory sign likely has legal force, but the batch does not state that regulatory signs must be obeyed.

statements.note: The exception appears in the same sign text, so it is written as an UNLESS clause.

statements.text: a driver MAY pass [?safely] on the side shown by the downward lines WHEN a warning sign shows downward lines

sources.quote: The downward lines show the side on which you may safely pass.

flags.note: No measure of safe passing is given.

statements.note: The sentence describes a sign but states what a driver may do, so it is written as a MAY rule.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass the pilot vehicle or the pace vehicle WHEN a pilot vehicle or the pace vehicle bears a "do not pass the pilot vehicle or pace vehicle bearing this sign" sign

sources.quote: a temporary condition sign
Do not pass the pilot vehicle or pace vehicle bearing this sign.

flags.note: A temporary condition sign likely has legal force, but the batch does not state that such signs must be obeyed.

statements.text: DEFINE long commercial vehicle IS a double trailer THAT can be up to 40 m in length

sources.quote: This placard indicates a long commercial vehicle, which is a double trailer and can be up to 40 metres in length.

flags.note: The handbook also uses the abbreviation LCV.

statements.text: FACT the long commercial vehicle placard indicates a long commercial vehicle

sources.quote: This placard indicates a long commercial vehicle, which is a double trailer and can be up to 40 metres in length.
Title: Long commercial vehicle (LCV) - Description: Long commercial vehicle (LCV)

statements.text: a driver SHOULD recognize a long commercial vehicle based on rear signage WHEN the driver is on the highway

sources.quote: It is important to be able to recognize an LCV on the highway, based on rear signage, and anticipate both the extended length and limited speed when preparing to pass one on the highway.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD anticipate the extended length of up to 40 m AND the [?limited] speed WHEN preparing to pass a long commercial vehicle on the highway

sources.quote: It is important to be able to recognize an LCV on the highway, based on rear signage, and anticipate both the extended length and limited speed when preparing to pass one on the highway.

flags.note: No speed limit or measure of limited speed is given.

statements.note: The 40 m length is taken from the definition in the same passage.

statements.text: FACT pavement markings tell a driver when it is not [?safe] to pass

sources.quote: Pavement markings divide traffic lanes, show turning lanes, mark pedestrian crossings, indicate obstacles and tell you when it is not safe to pass.

flags.note: The handbook does not define what makes passing safe or not safe; the marking is the indicator.

statements.note: Only the passing-relevant part of the sentence is extracted; the other functions of pavement markings (dividing lanes, showing turning lanes, marking crossings, indicating obstacles) are not about passing.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass WHEN there is a solid line at the left of the driver's lane BECAUSE it is [?unsafe] to pass

sources.quote: A solid line at the left of your lane means it is unsafe to pass. ('A' should not pass.)
vehicles travelling beside a solid yellow line

flags.note: The solid line is the indicator of unsafety; no separate measure is given.

statements.note: The figure (m22) shows vehicles beside a solid yellow line, illustrating the solid-line condition.

statements.text: a driver MAY pass WHEN there is a broken line at the left of the driver's lane AND the way is [?clear] AND there are [?enough] broken lines ahead to complete the pass [?safely]

sources.quote: A broken line at the left of your lane means you may pass if the way is clear. ('A' may pass if there are enough broken lines ahead to complete the pass safely.)
vehicles travelling beside broken yellow lines

flags.note: No precise definition of what makes the way clear.
No number of broken lines is given.
No measure of safety is given.

statements.note: The figure (m24) shows vehicles beside broken yellow lines, illustrating the broken-line condition.

statements.text: a driver MUST slow AND carefully pass a stopped emergency vehicle IF VIOLATED 3 demerit points

sources.quote: Failing to slow and carefully pass a stopped emergency vehicle

flags.note: No measure of care is given; the driver must judge what careful passing requires.

statements.note: The 3 demerit points come from the heading "Three points" of the Table of offences section.

statements.text: a driver MUST move into another lane WHEN passing a stopped emergency vehicle AND it is [?possible] IF VIOLATED 3 demerit points

sources.quote: Failing to move, where possible, into another lane when passing a stopped emergency vehicle

flags.note: Whether moving into another lane is possible depends on the driver's judgment of available space and traffic.

statements.note: The 3 demerit points come from the heading "Three points" of the Table of offences section. "Where possible" is expressed as a WHEN condition.

statements.force_from: context ("Sanctions – dangerous behaviours", page "Losing your licence")
statements.text: a driver MUST NOT drive a motor vehicle to prevent another vehicle from passing IF VIOLATED loss of licence

sources.quote: driving a motor vehicle to prevent another vehicle from passing

statements.note: The item is a bare noun phrase; the legal force and penalty come from the section context: it is listed as a dangerous behaviour under sanctions on the "Losing your licence" page.

statements.text: FACT a driver towing a trailer cannot accelerate as quickly

sources.quote: You cannot accelerate as quickly when you are towing a trailer.

statements.text: FACT a driver towing a trailer needs more space because the vehicle is much longer with a trailer attached

sources.quote: You also need more space because the length of your vehicle is much longer with a trailer attached.

statements.text: a driver towing a trailer SHOULD make sure there is [?enough] time and room to complete the pass WHEN the driver is about to pass a vehicle

sources.quote: Before you pass, make sure you have enough time and room to complete the pass.

flags.note: No measure of time or room is given.

statements.text: a driver towing a trailer SHOULD allow more room before moving back to the lane AND SHOULD NOT cut back into the lane [?too soon] WHEN the driver has passed a vehicle BECAUSE cutting back into the lane too soon can cause the trailer to sway and make it difficult to control

sources.quote: Once you have passed, allow more room before you move back to your lane. Do not cut back into the lane too soon. This can cause your trailer to sway and make it difficult to control.

flags.note: No measure of how soon is too soon is given.

statements.note: The two sentences are two sides of the same instruction (give space after passing), so they are joined as two actions in one statement.

statements.text: a driver towing a trailer SHOULD signal AND pull over AND let other vehicles pass WHEN the driver is holding up a line of traffic

sources.quote: If you are holding up a line of traffic, signal, pull over and let the other vehicles pass.

statements.text: FACT fast-moving trucks and buses create a strong air disturbance behind them

sources.quote: Fast-moving trucks and buses create a strong air disturbance behind them.

statements.text: FACT the wall of wind behind a large bus or truck may whip a driver's trailer to the side, pushing it out of control WHEN a large bus or truck passes the driver

sources.quote: If a large bus or truck passes you, the wall of wind behind it may whip your trailer to the side, pushing it out of control.

statements.text: a driver towing a trailer SHOULD NOT brake AND SHOULD carefully steer the vehicle and trailer back into position WHEN the trailer is whipped to the side by a large bus or truck passing the driver

sources.quote: If a large bus or truck passes you, the wall of wind behind it may whip your trailer to the side, pushing it out of control. When you experience this, do not brake. Carefully steer your vehicle and trailer back into position.

statements.note: The pronoun 'this' refers to the wall of wind whipping the trailer, so the preceding sentence is cited to define the condition.

statements.text: FACT a slight increase in speed may help WHEN the trailer is whipped to the side by a large bus or truck passing the driver

sources.quote: If a large bus or truck passes you, the wall of wind behind it may whip your trailer to the side, pushing it out of control. When you experience this, do not brake. Carefully steer your vehicle and trailer back into position. A slight increase in speed may help.

statements.note: "may help" states a possibility, not a permission, so this is a FACT.

statements.text: a driver MUST move to the right AND allow the other vehicle to pass WHEN the driver of another vehicle is about to overtake and pass the driver's vehicle

sources.quote: When the driver of another vehicle is about to overtake and pass your vehicle, you must:
Move to the right and allow such vehicle to pass.

statements.note: Extracted from a sample test question: m87 provides the condition and the legal force ("you must"), m88 provides the required action. Together they state the duty of the driver being passed.
